A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with asthma can maintain or regain control over the condition by using self-management skills to monitor and regulate their breathing.

patients with asthma who are involved in self-management programs can maintain their skills and use them over time and across a variety of settings, including those in which the skills were not originally taught.

self-management skills acquired in an educational program are maintained and used to varying degrees over time, even in the absence of asthma symptoms, and that patients continue to use self-management to monitor and prevent the return of symptoms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients who have been trained in self-management skills continue to use some of them over time, even after their asthma is in remission.
patients who are trained in asthma self-management skills are more likely to continue to use them over time, even when they are asymptomatic.
